children.text: Maasin Cathedral is the national shrine of Our Lady of the Assumption in Maasin City, Southern Leyte, and the seat of the Diocese of Maasin. Its history stretches from the Jesuit parish of 1700 through repeated destruction and rebuilding, and it makes a quiet stop for a look at the church and its plaza.

The official name of Maasin Cathedral is the National Shrine and Cathedral Parish of Our Lady of the Assumption. It is a Roman Catholic church in Maasin City, Southern Leyte, and the seat of the Diocese of Maasin. According to Wikipedia its coordinates are 10°7′58″N, 124°50′19″E, in the center of Maasin, and maps list it as "Maasin Cathedral" on Bishop Ataviado Street. Maasin is a city at the southern tip of Leyte island and the capital of Southern Leyte.

The Maasin parish is described as one of the oldest in the Philippines. The mission passed in turn from the Jesuits to the Augustinians and then the Franciscans. According to the record, the Jesuits formally established the parish here in 1700, and a stone inscription from a destroyed convent is cited as evidence. The first church was destroyed in 1754 in Moro (Muslim raider) attacks, and in 1771 the Augustinians built a second church at the present site, about
1 km
from the old ruins. That church was damaged again by raiders in 1784.

The Franciscans arrived in 1843 and made Our Lady of the Assumption the parish patroness on August 15, which is still Maasin's official feast day. After a fire in 1882, Filipino priests Fr. Toribio Padilla and Fr. Felix Magno led the reconstruction. When the Franciscans left during the Philippine Revolution in 1896, local clergy took over the parish, and on August 14, 1968 the church became the cathedral of the newly created Diocese of Maasin. The present building is described as dating from 1968, but how that fits with the record of completion in 1771 is explained differently by different sources and is not certain. More recently, the cathedral was heavily renovated in 2016–2018 ahead of the diocese's 50th anniversary, and Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle presided over the closing Mass of the 2018 Golden Jubilee. Typhoon Rai (Odette) in December 2021 shattered windows and forced a full roof replacement, and on August 14, 2024 the church was elevated to a national shrine. Its style is described as baroque, with a simple facade under a triangular pediment, rectangular niches for images and windows, and a rounded, layered bell tower typical of late-18th-century churches.

This guide is for travelers in southern Leyte who want to spend half a day in Maasin. The cathedral itself can be seen in an hour or two, so it combines well with other plans such as Limasawa Island or nearby waterfalls. Mass times and opening hours could not be confirmed and are given differently by different sources, so ask the parish before you go.

blocks.title: The statue of Our Lady of the Assumption

children.text: The patroness is Our Lady of the Assumption of Maasin (Nuestra Señora de la Asunción de Maasin), called "Mahal nga Patrona" locally. The old carved wooden statue, showing the Virgin on a cloud surrounded by cherubs, is fragile and kept in a separate chapel, while a dressed statue with an ivory head and hands is the current altar and processional image. After an episcopal coronation on August 15, 2018, Pope Francis granted a canonical coronation decree on December 14, 2021, and the papal nuncio crowned the image on August 13, 2022.

blocks.title: New main altar and side altars

children.text: In 2017 a new main altar backdrop was built, flanked by statues of the Archangel Michael and St. Vincent Ferrer, and new side altars were added in 2018. They include altars for Saints Peter and Paul, the Santo Niño de Limasawa, St. Joseph with the Child Jesus, St. Anthony of Padua and St. Padre Pio. On September 24, 2015, the old statue of Our Lady is said to have returned to the main altar under a new canopy.

Beside the church, Plaza Asunción has a large statue of Our Lady of the Assumption. It is said to be the former altar statue that was moved from inside the church to the plaza during the 2017 renovation. It is a good place to rest before or after going in and to photograph the facade and bell tower.

The Catholic Bishops' Conference of the Philippines announced the elevation on July 6, 2024, and Cardinal Jose Advincula presided over the rites on August 14. At the same time, the Shrine of Our Lady of Mercy in Novaliches, Quezon City, was also elevated.

blocks.title: Site of the old Jesuit convent

children.text: Traces of the site of the first Jesuit convent are said to lie between the Abgao and Mantahan districts. It is not a conspicuous ruin, so it is enough to know it as part of the history rather than going out of your way to find it.

blocks.title: The heart of the Diocese of Maasin

children.text: The Diocese of Maasin covers all of Southern Leyte plus Matalom, Bato, Hilongos, Hindang, Inopacan and Baybay, with an area of about
, 38 parishes and about 90 percent Catholics. Many people come and go between the cathedral and the diocesan offices, so the area can be busy at Mass times.

items.title: Half-day course
items.subtitle: The cathedral, the plaza and a walk downtown

children.text: Reach Maasin Cathedral by tricycle or on foot from your hotel and look at the facade and bell tower.
If it is not Mass time, go inside to see the main altar, the side altars and the statue of Our Lady of the Assumption.
Walk through the neighboring Plaza Asunción and rest in front of the large statue of Our Lady.
Have lunch at a restaurant or mall downtown.
Stroll around the port and downtown, or prepare for the next leg (waterfalls or Limasawa Island).
The inside of the church must be kept quiet during Mass, and its opening hours have not been confirmed. Visit outside Mass times.

items.title: Full-day course
items.subtitle: Combining the cathedral with nearby sights

children.text: Look around Maasin Cathedral.
Visit one or two of the sights listed for Maasin, such as the waterfalls or the Monte Cueva Shrine.
Return to town for lunch.
Limasawa Island requires a separate boat, so if your schedule is long it is better to leave it for the next day.
Many of the waterfalls and shrines are listed by name only, so confirm the location and how to get there locally first.
The nearest major airports from Manila are Daniel Z. Romualdez Tacloban Airport (TAC) and the airport at Ormoc. Airlines and schedules for Tacloban flights change with the season.
From Tacloban to Maasin, the van ride is described as taking about
3 hours
. The van terminals mentioned are Van-Van's, Duptours and the Tacloban New Transport terminal, but whether they are still current needs confirming.
Flight routes and van schedules change often, so check before you leave.

A fast ferry such as the Weesam Express is described as running between Cebu City and Maasin. Another option is to take a jeepney to Bato port and board a ferry to Cebu; an older source gives the fare as ₱290, so it may differ now.
Ferries linking Maasin with Ubay in Bohol and a Cokaliong route to Macrohon are also listed.
Philtranco is described as running two buses a day between Manila and Maasin via Tacloban and Legazpi. Check the schedule.
Buses and vans also connect from nearby Sogod, Baybay, Ormoc and Tacloban.
From the terminal you can walk to the cathedral or take a tricycle. Tricycles and motorcycle taxis (habal-habal) are described as the main means of transport in Maasin.
Searching for "Maasin Cathedral" on Google Maps makes the location easy to find.

Maasin lies in Southern Leyte, where some months are rainy and typhoons have caused damage. Viewing the church is little affected by weather, but the dry season is easier if you also plan nearby waterfalls and islands.

The busiest time is the feast of the Assumption on August 15. It is Maasin's official feast day and Masses and events follow one another, so avoid it if you want a quiet visit, and book lodging early if you want to see the festive atmosphere.

rows: Fine for walking around town, but prepare for rain at the tail end of the wet season

items.label: Accommodation
items.note: Older sources list places in the ₱150–700 range

Based on older sources, Maasin has places to stay such as GV Hotel, Ampil Pensionne, Southern Comfort Pensionne and DW Pensione. Rates were listed in the ₱150–700 range, but that information is old, so check current prices and reviews on a booking site. The church and the port are close, so staying downtown lets you get around on foot.

Downtown has Metro Gaisano (next to the bus terminal, with a supermarket and food court) and Prince Supermarket, and 24-hour ATMs at Metrobank and PNB are listed. Among the restaurants listed, Alberto's Pizza (Espina Street) is said to start at ₱80, but check locally whether it is still open. Most meals are taken at downtown restaurants or food courts.
Refrain from photography and loud talking during Mass, and dress with shoulders and knees covered.

Mass times differ by source. One travel blog says there is a Mass every day at 11 am, while the parish listing recommends inquiring. The parish numbers (053) 570-9712 and (053) 381-2079 have been listed, but check whether they are current.
Timing your visit for the August 15 feast gives the richest church and festival atmosphere, but lodging can run short, so book early.
The van from Tacloban takes about
3 hours
, so it is better to leave early in the morning.
St. Joseph College next to the church is listed as another place you can see on the same visit.
If you want to include Limasawa Island, boats can be canceled depending on the weather, so leave a day to spare.
Watch out for pickpockets and snatchers, and use bank ATMs or shopping malls downtown to exchange money.
No confirmed official information exists on the church's opening hours or Mass times. Ask the parish office before you go.
Repairs after the damage from Typhoon Rai in 2021 may have continued, so some areas may be restricted.
Much of the transport and fare information comes from older sources and may differ now.
Dates and the completion of the building differ by source, so rely on the signs and staff explanations.
During typhoon season, flights and boats can be canceled, so leave spare days in your schedule.
This island is described as where Magellan's party landed and held the first Catholic Mass in the Philippines, and you get there from Maasin by boat. Butuan makes the same claim, so accounts differ.
Busay Falls and Guinsohotan Falls are listed in the guide to Maasin. Check the locations and how to get there locally.
